title: Queen’s Tower amid the rebuild, 1962
summary: By 1962 the old Institute complex around Queen’s Tower was being taken apart piece by piece: demolition of the rear galleries had begun in 1957, and the east wing of the main range had already been replaced by a college building. The Institute itself had been renamed the Commonwealth Institute in 1958 and moved to Holland Park in 1962. The record is thin for this year — no usable dated reference images survive, and the exact condition of the west wing in 1962 is unresolved, so read this as an interim sketch rather than a finished picture.
funFacts: Demolition of the rear galleries began in 1957.
By 1962 the east wing of the main range had been replaced by a college building.
The Institute was renamed the Commonwealth Institute in 1958 and moved to Holland Park in 1962.
Making the central tower stand independently, with new foundations and substantial rebuilding of the lower portion, came in 1966–68.
The west wing was demolished by 1965, but the sources do not pin down its condition on any given day in 1962.

sources.title: Survey of London, Vol. 38: Queen’s Tower and the Imperial Institute
Imperial College: History of Queen’s Tower

sceneBrief.description: A tall Victorian campanile of pale stone rises from the middle of a partly dismantled Institute complex. The east side of the main frontage is a newer college building, not the original wing; there are no finished lawns or landscaped setting around the tower’s foot. Do not show the complete 1893 frontage, and do not show the isolated tower on its later foundations.

persists: The central tower’s upper structure, still unchanged.
altered: The surrounding Institute complex, being replaced by Imperial College buildings; the east wing has already gone.
notYetBuilt: The 1966–68 freestanding foundation and rebuilt lower structure of the tower.
gone: The pre-demolition east wing of the Institute frontage.

sceneBrief.surroundings: North: the tower standing amid campus redevelopment, with the rear galleries affected by demolition begun in 1957. East: a replacement college building on the former east-wing site. West: not established for 1962 — the sources only record demolition by 1965. South: the opposite frontage and its chronology are unverified. A full 360-degree reconstruction is not yet supported by this research.

guide.name: Alfred Nunn
guide.bio: I’ve been a porter at the college for going on twenty years, and I know every stair and doorway round here. These days I spend half my time pointing visitors away from the works and the other half telling them where the tower is.
guide.appearance: A man in his early sixties, stout and short, with a clean-shaven weathered face and grey hair under a peaked cap; he wears a dark heavy porter’s coat with brass buttons over a collar and tie, and sturdy worn boots.
guide.script: Alfred Nunn, college porter, at your service. Mind the mud as we go — there’s a fair bit of shifting about here lately. The galleries at the back have been coming down since 1957, and the east wing’s gone already, replaced with a college building. The Institute folk packed up their things and went off to Holland Park this year; they’d been the Commonwealth Institute since 1958. The tower stays put, mind. We’ve no proper images of the place from this year, so I can only tell you what I see with my own eyes. Now then, I must get back to the gate. Good day to you.
guide.greeting: Hallo there — Alfred Nunn, porter. You’ll want to mind your step round here, it’s all change about the old Institute.
